name: message
title: Message
purpose: One row of an agent transcript: the start of the session, a prompt, the agent's text, a question to the reader, a tool call, its result, an answered permission request, a denial, an error, usage or the end of a turn.
whenToUse: For each event of an agent's turn, as a list item in the transcript's ol or ul, oldest first.
To show what a tool was asked to do and what it returned, in mono, at phone width.
whenNotToUse: For a request that still waits for the reader's answer. Use an approval, which carries Allow and Decline.
For what the agent is doing right now, with Stop. Use the now-doing line under the transcript. For a note that work is going on somewhere else in a view, use streaming.
For a message about the app itself, such as a lost connection. Use an alert or a banner.

variants.name: agent
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. Text the agent wrote. Label it with the agent's name. While the text arrives the row carries data-state: streaming, stopped, interrupted, reconnecting or done.

variants.name: session-start
variants.use: A quiet first row saying that the session started, and where: the branch, the directory, the agent. Label it Session.

variants.name: user
variants.use: A prompt the reader sent. Label it You.

variants.name: question
variants.use: A question the agent asks the reader, when the run waits on the answer. Label it Question, waiting on you, and once it is answered label it Question and show the answer as the next user row. A request for permission to run something is not a question: use an approval.

variants.name: tool-call
variants.use: A tool the agent was asked to run. The row holds one thing: the tool call component with its row modifier, ds-tool-call ds-tool-call--row, and its data-state. That component draws the status, the plain summary written as what was done and not as raw JSON, the time, the agent's reason and the disclosure with the arguments and the output. This is the one way to show a tool call in a transcript. A row written the earlier way, with ds-message__label, ds-message__tool, ds-message__command and a ds-message__details element, is still drawn.

variants.name: tool-result
variants.use: What a tool returned, as a row of its own. A call shown with the tool call component keeps its output inside its own details, so a new transcript does not need this row. It stays for a result shown apart from its call: show the first lines, and put the rest in a details element whose summary reads Show full output.

variants.name: decision
variants.use: A permission request that was resolved. The label says how, in words beside an icon from the sprite in ds-message__icon: Allowed with check, Declined with x, Pre-approved with circle-check for a command on the task's approved list, or Allowed by a standing permission with circle-check. Then the tool and the command, then one sentence saying by whom and when: who allowed or declined it and their note, who set the approved list, or who granted the standing permission. For the last two, say that nobody was asked.

variants.name: denied
variants.use: A call the permission rules refused without asking. Say what was not run and why. For a request a person declined, use the decision row.

variants.name: error
variants.use: Something that failed: a tool that crashed, a lost connection, a limit reached. Say what failed, what state the work is in and what to do next. It is not for a refused call, which is the denied row.

variants.name: usage
variants.use: A quiet line of figures for the turn, such as tokens and duration.

variants.name: turn-end
variants.use: A quiet closing row under a rule, saying that the turn finished and how: completed, stopped or ended with an error.

accessibility: Each row is an li in an ol or ul. When rows are added while the reader watches, wrap the list in an element with role="log", aria-live="off" and an accessible name. The log role tells assistive technology what the region is, and aria-live="off" keeps it from reading every row and every word as it lands. What matters is announced from the view's one status region: see the activity announcer.

Every row but a tool call starts with ds-message__label, which says the kind in words: Session, You, Claude Code, Question, Tool result, Allowed, Declined, Pre-approved, Allowed by a standing permission, Denied, Error, Usage, End. A tool-call row holds the tool call component, whose line starts with its status in words. The kind is never the colour or an icon alone. The icons of the denied and error rows are drawn by the stylesheet, and the icon of an answered request is an svg with ds-message__icon and aria-hidden="true" inside the label.
A question row that waits says so in its label, Question, waiting on you. Once it is answered the label reads Question alone.

While the agent's text arrives, set data-state="streaming" and aria-busy="true" on the row, append to the text of ds-message__body without rebuilding it, and keep a span with ds-message__caret and aria-hidden="true" as its last child. Never put aria-live on the growing text. When the reply ends set data-state="done" and remove the caret and aria-busy.

When the reader stops the reply, keep the text that arrived, set data-state="stopped" and add a p with ds-message__state after the body that starts with the word Stopped. When the connection or the process is lost, set data-state="interrupted", say so in ds-message__state starting with the word Interrupted, and put a Retry button with ds-button ds-button--small after it. While the app tries to resume, set data-state="reconnecting" and say Reconnecting in ds-message__state: the text stays, and nothing is added twice. The stylesheet draws an icon beside each of the three from data-state.
Only the caret and the reconnecting mark move, and under prefers-reduced-motion both are still.
Write transcript text as text, never as markup, and write out characters that cannot be seen.

Collapsed arguments and long output use a native details element, with no script. Its summary holds text that says what is inside. Enter and Space open and close it, and its pointer target is as tall as a row: 40px by default and 44px on a coarse pointer.
When output is cut short, the lines after the preview go in the details element, so opened text continues where the preview stopped.
A transcript that is loading is a skeleton with aria-busy and a sentence for screen readers. An empty one is a compact empty state, with suggestion chips when there are prompts to offer.
The component needs no script. The app sets data-state and aria-busy on a row that streams, and the browser manages the open attribute.
